newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Reed shares slide as profit stalls.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Reed shares slide as profit stalls.

text.p: The strength of sterling cut Reed Elsevier's interim profits by 36 million pounds ($57.6 million) and the Anglo-Dutch publisher warned on Thursday of a similar hit in the second part of the year.
Pre-tax profit rose only one percent to 419 million pounds ($671 million) in the first six months but the company said profit would have increased 10 percent at constant exchange rates.
The profit figure was towards the bottom end of expectations and Reed shares in London fell five percent as analysts trimmed their full-year earnings forecasts.
Reed shares in London were 32p lower at 598p in mid-afternoon while Elsevier stock shed 2.00 guilders (94 cents) to 35.50 in Amsterdam.

Share analysts said Reed Elsevier, which has shed many of its consumer operations to focus on supplying specialist information in areas such as business and science, was well placed for future growth.

"Higher development costs and sterling are squeezing profits," said analyst Anthony de Larrinaga of broker Panmure Gordon. "The underlying position is very healthy. They have the content, the management and the resources."
De Larrinaga cut his 1997 pre-tax profit forecast by 30 million pounds to 840 million. Other analysts scaled back their estimates to the 830-840 million range.

Reed Elsevier co-chairman Herman Bruggink said returns on the investment in electronic publishing should begin to feed through by 1999 or 2000. The investment rose to 28 million guilders from 20 million a year before, he told a presentation in Amsterdam.
His English counterpart Nigel Stapleton told Reuters the impact of the pound would be only slightly lower in the second half if it remained at current levels.
Almost two thirds of Reed Elsevier's profit is derived from the U.S. dollar, Dutch guilder, Swiss franc and French franc but results are calculated in sterling.
Sales fell one percent to 1.664 billion pounds, although they were six percent higher at constant exchange rates.

The company said it remained 'positive' about prospects for the rest of 1997 and the longer-term. Stapleton said Reed Elsevier was prepared to spend a further two billion dollars on acquisitions after committing around one billion dollars so far in 1997.
"Growth by acquisition continues to be an important part of our strategic agenda...We are well up to speed with what might be available," he said.
Reed Elsevier's spending commitment takes account of the $447 million acquisition of U.S. business publisher Chilton, which is expected to be completed shortly.
Other big acquisitions this year include a $320 million deal for MDL Information Systems, a U.S. scientific software and information database company.
Reed Elsevier said its rate of margin growth would be constrained by the higher investment in electronic publishing initiatives and continuing difficulties at its Reed Travel Group arm.
Hard copy revenues from the travel arm are in decline and the company has embarked on a two-year investment programme to develop its online business.
